---
title: "Second half – The multiverse of the claim"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this half](../../live/eu-frames-short.html#/second-half-the-multiverse-of-the-claim){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

In the first half everyone who chose the same analyst reproduced the same number, because everyone ran the same code. In the second you become analyst number six and make choices of your own: you take the analysis apart into its decisions, try alternatives in the browser lab, send the analysis that you would defend to the class chart, and read the chart against the curve of every defensible analysis of the claim.

## 1. The specification menu

**On the slides**, with the specification menu open in another tab.

[Open the specification menu](../../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Fourteen decisions in three groups, "The question", "Measurement" and "The model", and the decisions of survey methodology among them: which items form a scale, the respondent who named nothing, the weights within a country-year and across them, the estimator, and inference with few clusters. The slides end on the ground rules: every try starts from the reproduced specification and changes one decision.

## 2. The code behind the menu

**On the slides.** Two slides show the code that the course runs: the datawizard verbs that build a specification from the panel, including the within–between model in one call, and `parameters::model_parameters()` reading the fitted model with its clustered errors, with the conversion rule of Multi100 as one call of effectsize.

## 3. Task 4 – The menu

[Open the browser lab at Task 4](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-explore){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

On the three slides of the hands-on, call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Then submit the one that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`; the lab holds the same cells as a page of the site. Your dot is drawn on the class chart of the [Multiverse page](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#class-results) as an exploratory result.

## 4. The multiverse and the class chart

**On the slides**, with the Multiverse page open in another tab.

[Open the Multiverse page](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The slides say where the idea of a multiverse comes from and how a menu of fourteen decisions was pruned to a curve of 864, and then set the dots of the class against the curve.

## 5. The bet and what moved the estimates

**On the slides.** Before the reveal, you bet on which decision moves the estimates most. The slides then show the decomposition by decision, and place the five analysts and the original study on the curve.

## 6. Your placement

[Open the browser lab at Task 4](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-explore){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

In the cell of the placement slide, rerun the specification that you submitted with `try_spec()`, read off your placement among the 864 specifications of the curve, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go. Without a submission of your own, use the placement of the reproduced specification, 67%.

## 7. Reading a curve

**On the slides**, with the page on reading a specification curve open in another tab.

[Open Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

What the curve describes and what it leaves out, why 864 estimates are not 864 tests, what the critics of multiverse analysis hold, and what preregistration settles.

## 8. Replication and the close

**On the slides.** The replication that SCORE ran on later waves of the Standard Eurobarometer returns with its verdict, and the three kinds of repetition return with this paper in their cells. The session closes on what you take with you and where to go next.

**By the end of the half** you have tried alternatives one decision at a time, your explored analysis is on the class chart with your placement among the 864, and you can say what the curve that you joined does and does not establish, next to a claim that held under every analysis of one dataset and was tested again on new data.
